# Automated Landmark Detection for Assessing Hip Conditions: MRI vs. X-ray (ISBI 2026)

> Automated Landmark Detection for Assessing Hip Conditions: A Cross-Modality Validation of MRI Versus X-Ray. Roberto Di Via, Vito Paolo Pastore, Francesca Odone, Siôn Glyn-Jones, Irina Voiculescu (MaLGa Center, DIBRIS, University of Genoa; Nuffield Department of Orthopaedics, Rheumatology and Musculoskeletal Sciences, University of Oxford; Department of Computer Science, University of Oxford). 2026 IEEE 23rd International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI), pp. 1-4. DOI 10.1109/ISBI61048.2026.11515938.

This is the first cross-modality validation of automated hip landmark detection between X-ray and MRI for femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) assessment. A UNet++ with an ImageNet-initialised ResNet18 encoder is trained by heatmap regression (Gaussian targets, NLL loss, 512x512 inputs, test-time augmentation) to localise four landmarks (femoral head centre, neck-axis point, lateral acetabular edge, lateral cam point), from which the alpha angle and the lateral centre-edge (LCE) angle are computed. Data: 89 patients from the FAIT trial (Oxford) with paired AP pelvic X-rays and T1-weighted coronal MRI (middle slice, index 10).

Key results (mean ± std over three runs):
- Overall mean radial error: 2.98±0.23 mm on MRI vs. 3.02±0.10 mm on X-ray.
- SDR@2/3/4 mm: MRI 58.3/73.5/83.1%, X-ray 62.5/79.2/85.4%.
- Cam-type impingement screening (alpha > 65°): 87.5% accuracy on both modalities, 100% specificity, 54.55% sensitivity.
- LCE-angle ICC(2,1): 0.82 (X-ray), 0.73 (MRI); MRI has narrower Bland-Altman limits of agreement for LCE (±10.5° vs. ±21.6°).
